category: PSpice measurement definitions (goal functions) and the search-command language
description: The predefined measurement definitions shipped in PSpice.prb (the list in the PSpice 17.4 help, 'Measurement Definitions Included with PSpice'), used with Trace > Evaluate Measurement, View > Measurement Results, Performance Analysis and PSpice Advanced Analysis, plus the syntax for writing custom definitions: marked point expressions, MPAVG, comment tags and the Search command with its LEvel, SLope, PEak, TRough, MAx, MIn, POint and XValue conditions. Argument names shown follow PSpice.prb conventions (1 = trace argument, begin_x/end_x = X range, db_level, n_occur); the authoritative argument list and #Arg# comments for your release are shown by Trace > Measurements > View.

tools.name: Bandwidth (measurement)
tools.description: Returns the bandwidth of a band-pass shaped response at a user-chosen number of dB below its maximum, as x2 - x1 of the rising and falling crossings. The trace argument must already be in dB (for example VDB(out) or DB(V(out))).

parameters.description: Trace in dB.

parameters.name: db_level
parameters.description: Number of dB below the maximum at which bandwidth is measured.

tools.notes: Defined in the help as bandwidth(1, db_level) = x2 - x1. For a low-pass response use Cutoff_Lowpass_3dB instead, because there is no lower crossing.

tools.name: Bandwidth_Bandpass_3dB (measurement)
tools.description: Returns the 3 dB bandwidth of a band-pass response. It uses the ForceDBArg1 mechanism so the argument can be a plain (non-dB) trace such as V(out); PSpice converts it to dB internally before searching for the two crossings 3 dB below the peak.

parameters.description: AC trace, linear or dB.

tools.notes: Fails (no result) when the response does not fall 3 dB on both sides inside the swept frequency range; widen the AC sweep.

tools.name: Bandwidth_Bandpass_3dB_XRange (measurement)
tools.description: Same as Bandwidth_Bandpass_3dB but restricts the search to an X range, which isolates one passband of a multi-resonant response or excludes spurious peaks.

parameters.name: begin_x
parameters.description: Start of the X range (Hz).

parameters.name: end_x
parameters.description: End of the X range (Hz).

tools.name: CenterFrequency (measurement)
tools.description: Returns the centre frequency of a band-pass response, taken midway between the crossings at the given dB level below the maximum. CenterFrequency_XRange adds begin_x and end_x arguments to confine the search.

parameters.name: db_level
parameters.description: dB below the peak defining the band edges.

tools.notes: The midpoint is arithmetic on the X values; for a geometric centre on log sweeps compute SQRT(x1*x2) in a custom definition.

tools.name: ConversionGain (measurement)
tools.description: Ratio of the maximum of the first waveform to the maximum of the second, used for mixer conversion gain or amplifier peak gain from two traces. ConversionGain_XRange limits both searches to an X range.

parameters.description: Output trace.
Reference (input) trace.

tools.name: Cutoff_Highpass_3dB (measurement)
tools.description: Returns the -3 dB cut-off frequency of a high-pass response. Like Bandwidth_Bandpass_3dB it forces the argument to dB, so V(out) can be passed directly. Cutoff_Highpass_3dB_XRange adds begin_x/end_x.

parameters.description: AC trace of the filter output.

tools.name: Cutoff_Lowpass_3dB (measurement)
tools.description: Returns the -3 dB cut-off (upper band edge) of a low-pass response relative to its maximum; the standard way to read amplifier or filter bandwidth from an AC sweep. Cutoff_Lowpass_3dB_XRange adds begin_x/end_x.

parameters.description: AC trace of the output.

tools.example: Cutoff_Lowpass_3dB(V(out))   in Performance Analysis versus a swept compensation capacitor

tools.name: DutyCycle (measurement)
tools.description: Duty cycle of the first complete pulse/period of a time-domain waveform, high time divided by period, using mid-level crossings. DutyCycle_XRange measures the first period inside an X range, which avoids start-up cycles.

parameters.description: Periodic transient trace.

tools.notes: Returns a fraction, not a percentage, in the stock definition; multiply by 100 if needed.

tools.name: Falltime_NoOvershoot (measurement)
tools.description: Fall time of a negative-going edge that has no overshoot, measured between the 90 % and 10 % points of the full Y range. Use it for clean digital-like edges.

parameters.description: Transient trace containing the falling edge.

tools.notes: With undershoot or ringing the percentage levels are computed from the wrong extremes; use Falltime_StepResponse.

tools.name: Falltime_StepResponse (measurement)
tools.description: Fall time of a negative-going step response that may ring or undershoot, referenced to the initial and final values rather than the absolute extremes. Falltime_StepResponse_XRange confines it to an X range.

parameters.description: Transient step response.

tools.name: GainMargin (measurement)
tools.description: Gain in dB at the first frequency where the phase reaches -180 degrees, i.e. the loop gain margin read from an AC sweep of the loop gain. It takes two expression arguments, a dB magnitude trace and a phase trace of the same loop-gain quantity.

parameters.description: Loop gain in dB, e.g. DB(V(fb)/V(err)).
Loop gain phase in degrees, e.g. P(V(fb)/V(err)).

tools.notes: Some help pages show the example with the phase trace first (GainMargin(Vp(Out),VdB(Out))); check the #Arg1#/#Arg2# comments with Trace > Measurements > View for your release. A negative result means gain is still below 0 dB at -180 degrees (stable); the margin is its magnitude.

tools.name: PhaseMargin (measurement)
tools.description: Phase margin of a loop-gain response: the phase distance from -180 degrees at the frequency where the gain crosses 0 dB. It needs both the dB magnitude and the phase trace of the loop gain, typically from a Middlebrook or Tian injection setup.

parameters.description: Loop gain magnitude in dB.
Loop gain phase in degrees.

tools.notes: If the phase is unwrapped past -360 degrees the result can be off by 360; verify on the plot. Confirm argument order via Trace > Measurements > View.

tools.name: Max (measurement)
tools.description: Maximum Y value of the waveform, returned as a single number per data section. It is the measurement counterpart of the MAX() trace function and the one to use in Performance Analysis, Sensitivity or Monte Carlo.

parameters.description: Any trace.

tools.example: Max(V(out))   or   Max(W(Q1)) as an Advanced Analysis Smoke-style check

tools.name: Max_XRange (measurement)
tools.description: Maximum Y value within a specified X range, used to ignore start-up transients or to measure a peak inside one window of time or frequency.

parameters.name: begin_x
parameters.description: Start of the range.

parameters.name: end_x
parameters.description: End of the range.

tools.name: Min (measurement)
tools.description: Minimum Y value of the waveform as a single number per section. Used for undershoot, dropout and minimum-supply checks.

parameters.description: Any trace.

tools.name: Min_XRange (measurement)
tools.description: Minimum Y value within a specified X range, for example the droop during a load step window only.

parameters.name: begin_x
parameters.description: Start of the range.

parameters.name: end_x
parameters.description: End of the range.

tools.name: NthPeak (measurement)
tools.description: Y value of the waveform at its n-th peak, where a peak is a local maximum. Used for ringing analysis (second overshoot, decay ratio) and oscillator start-up.

parameters.name: n_occur
parameters.description: Which peak to report (1 = first).

tools.name: Peak (measurement)
tools.description: Value of the waveform at its n-th peak; listed in the help with the same description as NthPeak and kept for compatibility with older .prb files.

parameters.name: n_occur
parameters.description: Peak occurrence number.

tools.name: Overshoot (measurement)
tools.description: Percentage overshoot of a step response, peak excursion beyond the final value relative to the step amplitude. Overshoot_XRange measures it inside an X range so a single step in a longer stimulus can be isolated.

parameters.description: Transient step response.

tools.example: Overshoot(V(out))  used in Performance Analysis versus compensation capacitance
tools.notes: The final value is taken from the end of the trace, so simulate long enough for settling.

tools.name: Period (measurement)
tools.description: Period of a time-domain periodic signal from successive same-direction mid-level crossings. Period_XRange measures within an X range, useful once an oscillator has stabilised.

parameters.description: Periodic transient trace.

tools.name: PowerDissipation_mW (measurement)
tools.description: Total power dissipation in milliwatts during the final period of a time-domain run. Its first argument is meant to be the integral of power (for example S(W(R1))), and the second the period, so the result is energy per period divided by the period.

parameters.description: Running integral of power, e.g. S(W(M1)).

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Length of the final interval in seconds.

tools.name: Pulsewidth (measurement)
tools.description: Width of the first pulse of a waveform measured between mid-level crossings. Pulsewidth_XRange measures the first pulse inside an X range.

parameters.description: Pulse waveform.

tools.name: Q_Bandpass (measurement)
tools.description: Quality factor of a band-pass response, centre frequency divided by bandwidth at the specified dB level. Q_Bandpass_XRange adds an X range for multi-peak responses.

parameters.name: db_level
parameters.description: dB below peak for the band edges (3 for classic Q).

tools.name: Risetime_NoOvershoot (measurement)
tools.description: 10 % to 90 % rise time of a positive-going edge with no overshoot. The help uses it as the worked example: search forward for the 10 % crossing (point 1), then the 90 % crossing (point 2), result x2 - x1.

parameters.description: Transient trace with a rising edge.

tools.notes: Percentages are of the full Y range of the trace, so ringing or overshoot corrupts the reference levels; use Risetime_StepResponse for underdamped edges.

tools.name: Risetime_StepResponse (measurement)
tools.description: Rise time of a step response that may overshoot, referenced to the initial and final values. Risetime_StepResponse_XRange confines the measurement to one step within a longer run.

parameters.description: Transient step response.

tools.name: SettlingTime (measurement)
tools.description: Time from a given begin_x until a step response settles within a specified band around its final value. SettlingTime_XRange also bounds the search at the end, which is needed when the stimulus contains several steps.

parameters.name: band
parameters.description: Allowed error band around the final value.

parameters.name: begin_x
parameters.description: Time at which the step is applied.

tools.notes: Check the argument order with Trace > Measurements > View; the band is in trace units in the stock definition.

tools.name: SlewRate_Fall (measurement)
tools.description: Slew rate of a negative-going step response in Y units per X unit (V/s for voltage versus time). SlewRate_Fall_XRange restricts it to an X range.

parameters.description: Transient trace with a falling edge.

tools.name: SlewRate_Rise (measurement)
tools.description: Slew rate of a positive-going step response, the standard op-amp large-signal speed figure. SlewRate_Rise_XRange restricts it to an X range.

parameters.description: Transient trace with a rising edge.

tools.name: Swing_XRange (measurement)
tools.description: Difference between the maximum and minimum of the waveform within an X range, i.e. peak-to-peak value. It is the usual ripple or output-swing measurement.

parameters.name: begin_x
parameters.description: Start of the range.

parameters.name: end_x
parameters.description: End of the range.

tools.example: Swing_XRange(V(out),9m,10m)   (output ripple over the last millisecond)

tools.name: XatNthY (measurement)
tools.description: X value (time or frequency) at the n-th occurrence of the waveform reaching a given Y value, in either direction. Typical uses are propagation delay, threshold crossing time and unity-gain frequency.

parameters.name: Y_value
parameters.description: Level to cross.

parameters.name: n_occur
parameters.description: Occurrence number (1 = first).

tools.notes: Measurements cannot be nested inside each other; combine results arithmetically in the Evaluate Measurement expression instead.

tools.name: XatNthY_PositiveSlope / XatNthY_NegativeSlope (measurement)
tools.description: X value at the n-th crossing of Y_value in the rising (positive slope) or falling (negative slope) direction only. They avoid counting the wrong edge when a signal crosses the level both ways each cycle.

parameters.name: Y_value
parameters.description: Level to cross.

parameters.name: n_occur
parameters.description: Occurrence number of that edge direction.

tools.notes: The help lists the rising version as 'XatNthY_Positive Slope' with a stray space; the definition name itself has no space.

tools.name: XatNthY_PercentYRange (measurement)
tools.description: X value at the n-th occurrence of the waveform crossing a percentage of its full Y range, specifically Y = Ymin + (Ymax - Ymin) * Y_pct / 100. It makes threshold-based timing independent of absolute signal levels.

parameters.name: Y_pct
parameters.description: Percentage of the full Y range.

parameters.name: n_occur
parameters.description: Occurrence number.

tools.name: YatX (measurement)
tools.description: Y value of the waveform at a given X value, e.g. gain at 1 kHz or output voltage at a given time. It is the most used building block for spot measurements in Sensitivity and Monte Carlo.

parameters.name: X_value
parameters.description: X position (s, Hz or sweep units).

tools.name: YatX_PercentXRange (measurement)
tools.description: Y value of the waveform at a given percentage of the X-axis range, so the same definition works regardless of the absolute run length or sweep limits.

parameters.name: X_pct
parameters.description: Position as a percentage of the X range (0-100).

tools.name: YatFirstX / YatLastX (measurement)
tools.description: Y value at the beginning or at the end of the X range. YatLastX applied to AVG() or RMS() traces returns the average or RMS value over the whole run as a number, which is a common idiom for efficiency and dissipation checks.

parameters.description: Any trace expression.

tools.name: ZeroCross (measurement)
tools.description: X value where the waveform first crosses zero. ZeroCross_XRange finds the first zero crossing inside an X range. Useful for resonance on IMG() of an impedance, or zero-crossing timing of AC waveforms.

parameters.description: Trace expected to cross zero.

tools.name: Measurement definition syntax
tools.description: A measurement definition is a name with expression arguments (1..n) and optional substitution arguments, a marked point expression computing the result, and a braced block of numbered search commands, one per expression argument, each ending with a semicolon. Comment lines start with * and the special tags *#Desc#* and *#Arg1#* feed the dialog boxes. Definitions live in the [Measurement Functions] section of a .prb file.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Up to 50 alphanumeric/underscore characters, starting with a letter.

parameters.name: subarg
parameters.description: Text placeholders (e.g. db_level) replaced by numbers at evaluation time and substituted into the search commands.

parameters.name: !n
parameters.description: Marks the point found by the preceding search as point n (x1/y1 ...).

tools.notes: Always end the last search command with a semicolon. Create new definitions with Trace > Measurements > New (or Copy an existing one) and store them in the local .prb so they travel with the design.

tools.name: Marked point expressions and MPAVG()
tools.description: The right-hand side of a measurement definition: a single real value computed from marked point coordinates x1, y1, x2, y2 ... using arithmetic operators and single-point functions such as ABS(), SGN(), SIN() and SQRT(). Multi-point functions (d(), s(), AVG(), RMS(), MIN(), MAX()) and complex functions (M(), P(), R(), IMG(), G()) are not allowed; the extra MPAVG function averages Y between two marked X points.

parameters.name: MPAVG p1,p2
parameters.description: Marked X points bounding the range.

parameters.name: .fraction
parameters.description: Fraction of the range, centred on its midpoint, to average over (default 1).

tools.name: Search command (cursor and measurement search syntax)
tools.description: The command that locates a point on a trace, used both to position a cursor (Trace > Cursor > Search Commands) and inside measurement definitions. Optional direction, start point, consecutive-point count, X/Y range and repeat count precede exactly one condition; keywords are case-insensitive and only the first two letters of a condition are required.

parameters.name: /start_point/
parameters.description: ^ or Begin = first point, $ or End = last point, or a marked point expression such as x1; default is the current point.

parameters.name: #consecutive_points#
parameters.description: Points required to confirm a condition (default 1); e.g. a peak must be higher than that many neighbours on each side.

parameters.name: (range_x[,range_y])
parameters.description: Floating values, percentages or marked points, e.g. (1n,200n), (5m,1,10%,90%), (,,1,3), (,30n).

parameters.name: repeat:
parameters.description: Which occurrence, e.g. 2:LEvel finds the second level crossing; if too large the last one found is used.

tools.notes: Forward means increasing X expression order, which can look backward on a reversed axis. If the condition is not found the cursor does not move and the measurement returns no value.

tools.name: LEvel(value[,posneg]) (search condition)
tools.description: Finds the next crossing of a Y level, interpolating an artificial point between data points when needed. The level can be absolute, a percentage of full range, a marked point expression, relative to the start value or to max/min, optionally in dB, which is how 3 dB points are expressed.

parameters.name: value forms
parameters.description: 1e5 | 50% | x1, y1, (x1-x2)/2 | .-3, .+3 (relative to start value) | .-3db | max-3, min+3 | max-3db, min+3db.

parameters.name: posneg
parameters.description: P positive-going, N negative-going, B both (default).

tools.example:
Search forward level(max-3db, n) !2
sfle(10v)   (cursor to Y = 10 V)
tools.notes: With #consecutive_points# > 1, that many following points minus one must stay on the same side for the crossing to count, which filters noise.

tools.name: SLope / PEak / TRough / MAx / MIn / POint / XValue (search conditions)
tools.description: The remaining search conditions: SLope finds the next maximum slope (P, N or B, default P) and marks a point halfway between the two defining samples; PEak and TRough find the nearest local maximum or minimum; MAx and MIn find the global extreme in the range (unaffected by direction, count or repeat); POint steps to the next data point; XValue(value) finds the first point at a given X.
tools.usage: SLope[(P|N|B)]  |  PEak  |  TRough  |  MAx  |  MIn  |  POint  |  XValue(<value>)

parameters.name: XValue value
parameters.description: Floating value, percentage of range, marked point expression, or relative/dB forms like LEvel.

tools.example:
Search forward xvalue(1k) !1
Search forward 2:peak !1
Search forward (0,10m) max !1
tools.notes: XValue ignores direction, consecutive points, range and repeat. MAx returns the nearest of equal maxima.

tools.name: sfxv() / sfle() / sbxv() / sble() (cursor search shorthands)
tools.description: Abbreviated Search Commands for moving the active cursor: sfxv(x) searches forward to an X value, sfle(y) forward to a Y level, and sbxv()/sble() do the same backward from the current cursor position. Typed in Trace > Cursor > Search Commands (Shift+Ctrl+S) with the cursor displayed.
tools.example: Trace > Cursor > Display, then Search Commands: sfxv(10ns)  or  sfle(10v)
tools.notes: Cursor movements are not recorded by File > Log Commands, so use search commands (or measurements) for repeatable automation.

tools.name: Trace > Measurements (Measurements dialog)
tools.description: Manages measurement definitions: New starts from a template, Copy duplicates an existing definition for editing, View shows the marked point expression, search function and comments, Edit modifies, Delete removes permanently, Eval evaluates a definition against a trace, and Load reads only the measurement section of another .prb file.
tools.usage: Trace > Measurements...  (New | Copy | View | Edit | Delete | Eval | Load)

parameters.name: Local file
parameters.description: Store the new definition in the design-local .prb (recommended).

parameters.name: Eval
parameters.description: Opens Arguments for Measurement Evaluation and displays the marked points graphically.

tools.example: Trace > Measurements > select Risetime_NoOvershoot > Copy > name Risetime_2080 > Edit levels to 20% and 80% > OK
tools.notes: Deleted definitions cannot be undeleted. Measurements are not supported while the plot is in Fourier mode.

tools.name: View > Measurement Results (Measurement Results table)
tools.description: Spreadsheet below the plot listing measurement expressions added with Trace > Evaluate Measurement; ticking the Evaluate column computes the value for the current data, and new measurements can be added directly in the table. For multi-section data it also reports statistics across runs.
tools.usage: View > Measurement Results; Trace > Evaluate Measurement to add rows

parameters.name: Evaluate
parameters.description: Check box that triggers evaluation of the row.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: Computed result.

tools.example: Trace > Evaluate Measurement > Cutoff_Lowpass_3dB(V(out)) > OK, then read the Value column; restrict data first with Plot > Axis Settings > X Axis > Use Data > Restricted.
tools.notes: Measurements applied to a restricted X data range (Axis Settings > User Defined data range) use only that data.
